items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: if f(x) = axⁿ then f′(x) = naxⁿ⁻¹, for any rational n. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which notation means the derivative of y with respect to x?
items.markingKey: D. dy/dx is Leibniz notation for the derivative.

items.stem: The graph of y = f′(x) is a parabola that crosses the x-axis at x = 2 and x = 5 and is positive between them. On which interval is f decreasing?
items.markingKey: A. f is decreasing where f′(x) < 0, i.e. outside [2, 5]; of the options only x > 5 lies there.

items.stem: Diego says that the normal to y = −x³ − x² − 3x + 6 at x = 3 has gradient 36. Explain the error and state the correct gradient of the normal.
items.markingKey: Tangent gradient −36 (A1); the normal is perpendicular so m₁m₂ = −1 (R1); gradient −1/(−36) = 1/36, not just the negative (A1).

items.stem: Explain why |x| is not differentiable at x = 0.
items.answer: For h > 0 the difference quotient (|h| − 0)/h = 1, for h < 0 it is −1; the one-sided limits differ, so the limit does not exist.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: For h > 0 the difference quotient (|h| − 0)/h = 1, for h < 0 it is −1; the one-sided limits differ, so the limit does not exist. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Briefly explain why the derivative of f(x) + g(x) is f′(x) + g′(x).
items.answer: The limit of a sum is the sum of the limits, so the difference quotient of f + g splits into the difference quotients of f and of g.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The limit of a sum is the sum of the limits, so the difference quotient of f + g splits into the difference quotients of f and of g. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: P(t) is the population of bacteria in a culture, in thousands, after t hours. Interpret the statement P′(14) = 10 in context, including units.
items.answer: At t = 14, P is increasing at a rate of 10 thousand bacteria per hour.
items.markingKey: Instantaneous rate of change at t = 14 (R1); increasing (A1); magnitude 10 with units thousand bacteria per hour (A1).

items.stem: For f(x) = 2x³ + 3x² + 8, determine whether f is increasing or decreasing at x = −2, explaining your reasoning.
items.markingKey: f′(x) = 6x² + 6x (A1); f′(−2) = 12 (A1), which is positive so f is increasing (R1).

items.stem: Explain why you need both f(a) and f′(a) to write down the tangent at x = a.
items.answer: A line needs a point and a gradient: f(a) gives the point (a, f(a)) and f′(a) gives the gradient.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: A line needs a point and a gradient: f(a) gives the point (a, f(a)) and f′(a) gives the gradient. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Differentiate f(x) = 3x² + 4x − 2 from first principles.
items.markingKey: (f(x + h) − f(x))/h set up (M1); f(x + h) correctly expanded (A1); simplified to 3h + 6x + 4 after cancelling h (A1); limit as h → 0: 6x + 4 (A1).

items.stem: The curve y = −4∛x − 5x√x passes through a point P with x = 8. Find the exact gradient of the curve at P.
Find lim(x→2) (x² − 3x + 2)/(x² − 3x + 2).
items.markingKey: Both numerator and denominator are 0 at x = 2 (R1); factorise: (x − 2)(x − (1))/((x − 2)(x − (1))) (M1 A1); cancel and substitute: 1 (A1).

items.stem: Mateo writes: "If f′(2) = 0 then f has a maximum or a minimum at x = 2." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Not necessarily: f(x) = x³ has f′(0) = 0 but a stationary point of inflection; the sign of f′ must change.
items.markingKey: Not necessarily: f(x) = x³ has f′(0) = 0 but a stationary point of inflection; the sign of f′ must change. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Find the equation of the tangent to y = 8∛x − x at x = 2.3, giving the gradient and intercept to 3 significant figures.
The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 3 for x ≤ 1 and f(x) = mx + c for x > 1. Given that f is differentiable at x = 1, find m and c.
items.markingKey: Differentiable ⇒ gradients agree: 2(1)(1) = m (M1) m = 2 (A1); continuous ⇒ values agree: −2 = 2(1) + c (M1); c = −4 (A1).

items.stem: "d/dx (1/x³) = 1/(3x²)." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.markingKey: Write x⁻³: derivative −3x⁻⁴ = −3/x⁴. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Let f(x) = 3x³ + 4x. The points P and Q on the graph of f have x-coordinates −1 and −1 + h respectively.
(a) Show that the gradient of the chord PQ is 3h² − 9h + 13.
(b) Hence find f′(−1), explaining your reasoning.
(c) Find the equation of the tangent to the graph at P.
items.markingKey: (a) f(−1 + h) expanded (M1 A1); subtract f(−1) = −7 and divide by h (M1) AG. (b) as h → 0 the chord gradient → 13 (R1 A1). (c) y + 7 = 13(x + 1) (M1) y = 13x + 6 (A1).

items.stem:
A function f has gradient function f′(x) = (x − 1)(x + 1)².
(a) Find the x-coordinates of the stationary points of f.
(b) Determine the nature of each stationary point, justifying your answer.
(c) Find f″(x) and verify that f″ is zero at one of the stationary points.
items.answer: (a) x = 1, x = −1 (b) x = 1: local minimum; x = −1: stationary point of inflection (c) f″(x) = 3x² + 2x − 1; f″(−1) = 0
items.markingKey: (a) f′(x) = 0 (M1) A1 A1 (b) sign of f′ changes − to + at x = 1 (R1 A1); (x − (−1))² ≥ 0 so no sign change at x = −1 (R1 A1) (c) differentiate (M1) A1; substitute (A1) [Total 10 marks]

items.stem:
The point P(3, 3) lies on the graph of f(x) = 9/x.
(a) Find the gradient of the curve at P.
(b) Find the equation of the tangent at P.
(c) The tangent meets the x-axis at A and the y-axis at B. Find the coordinates of A and B.
(d) Find the area of triangle OAB, where O is the origin.
(e) Find the equation of the normal at P.
items.markingKey: (a) dy/dx = −9/x² (M1), m = −1 (A1) (b) P(3, 3) (A1); y − 3 = −1(x − 3) (M1) y = 6 − x (A1) (c) set y = 0 and x = 0 (M1) A1 A1 (d) ½ × 6 × 6 (M1) = 18 (A1) (e) gradient 1 (A1); y = x (A1) [Total 12 marks]

items.stem:
This question is about differentiation from first principles.
(a) Show that (√(x + h) − √x)/h = 1/(√(x + h) + √x).
(b) Hence differentiate f(x) = 2√x from first principles.
(c) Explain why f is not differentiable at x = 0.
items.answer: (a) shown (b) f′(x) = 1/√x (c) the difference quotient k/√h → ∞ as h → 0⁺
items.markingKey: (a) multiply by the conjugate √(x + h) + √x (M1); numerator h (A1) AG (b) limit as h → 0 (M1) A1 (c) R1 R1 [Total 6 marks]

items.stem: If f(x) = 6x^(2/3), then f′(x) =
Which of the following best describes "gradient of a chord"?
options: Finding the derivative directly from the definition f′(x) = lim(h→0) (f(x + h) − f(x))/h
The average rate of change (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) between two points on a curve
The limit lim(h→0) (f(a + h) − f(a))/h exists (left and right limits agree)
If f(x) = axⁿ then f′(x) = naxⁿ⁻¹, for any rational n
items.answer: The average rate of change (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) between two points on a curve
items.markingKey: B. "gradient of a chord" is the average rate of change (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) between two points on a curve.

items.stem: If f′(x) < 0 for 1 < x < 4, then on that interval f is
items.markingKey: C. A negative gradient means the function is decreasing.

items.stem: Omar says that the normal to y = 2x³ − 5x² + 6x − 4 at x = −1 has gradient −22. Explain the error and state the correct gradient of the normal.
items.markingKey: Tangent gradient 22 (A1); the normal is perpendicular so m₁m₂ = −1 (R1); gradient −1/(22) = −1/22, not just the negative (A1).

items.stem: Rafael writes: "In first principles, (f(x + h) − f(x))/h with h = 0 gives f′(x)." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Substituting h = 0 gives 0/0; the limit as h → 0 is taken after cancelling h.
items.markingKey: Substituting h = 0 gives 0/0; the limit as h → 0 is taken after cancelling h. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Lars differentiates y = 2/√x and writes dy/dx = 2/(√x/2). Explain the error and give the correct derivative.
items.markingKey: The term must be written in index form 2/√x before using the power rule (R1); bring down the power −1/2 and reduce the index by 1 (M1); −1/x^(3/2) (A1).

items.stem: Explain why lim(x→3) (x² − 9)/(x − 3) exists even though the expression is undefined at x = 3.
items.answer: For x ≠ 3 it simplifies to x + 3, whose values approach 6 as x → 3; the limit depends on nearby values, not on the value at 3.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: For x ≠ 3 it simplifies to x + 3, whose values approach 6 as x → 3; the limit depends on nearby values, not on the value at 3. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain how the graph of y = f′(x) shows where f is increasing.
items.answer: f is increasing exactly where f′(x) > 0, i.e. where the graph of y = f′(x) lies above the x-axis.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: f is increasing exactly where f′(x) > 0, i.e. where the graph of y = f′(x) lies above the x-axis. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Briefly explain why the gradient of the normal is −1/f′(a).
items.answer: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, and perpendicular lines (neither vertical) have gradients whose product is −1.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, and perpendicular lines (neither vertical) have gradients whose product is −1. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Differentiate f(x) = −x² − 4x − 5 from first principles.
items.markingKey: (f(x + h) − f(x))/h set up (M1); f(x + h) correctly expanded (A1); simplified to −h − 2x − 4 after cancelling h (A1); limit as h → 0: −2x − 4 (A1).

items.stem: Find f′(x) given that f(x) = −2√x + 4x⁴ + 4x² + 9.
items.markingKey: Rewrite in index form (M1); differentiate term by term: 16x³ + 8x − 1/√x (A1 per correct term, up to 3).

items.stem: Find lim(x→1) (x² − 3x + 2)/(x² + 4x − 5).
items.markingKey: Both numerator and denominator are 0 at x = 1 (R1); factorise: (x − 1)(x − (2))/((x − 1)(x − (−5))) (M1 A1); cancel and substitute: −1/6 (A1).

items.stem: The function f(x) = x³ + x² + kx + 1 is increasing for all real x. Find the set of possible values of k.
items.markingKey: f′(x) = 3x² + 2x + k ≥ 0 for all x (M1); discriminant ≤ 0 (M1): 4 − 12k ≤ 0 (A1); k ≥ 1/3 (A1).

items.stem: Find the equation of the normal to the curve y = 4x² − 2x − 3 at the point where x = 1.
items.markingKey: y-coordinate −1 (A1); dy/dx = 8x − 2 (M1), gradient at x = 1: 6 (A1); normal gradient −1/6 (M1); y = −x/6 − 5/6 (A1).

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 1 − 3x² for x ≤ 2 and f(x) = mx + c for x > 2. Given that f is differentiable at x = 2, find m and c.
items.markingKey: Differentiable ⇒ gradients agree: 2(−3)(2) = m (M1) m = −12 (A1); continuous ⇒ values agree: −11 = −12(2) + c (M1); c = 13 (A1).

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the point on the curve y = −2x² − 6x at which the gradient is 1.

Let f(x) = x³ + 3x. The points P and Q on the graph of f have x-coordinates 2 and 2 + h respectively.
(a) Show that the gradient of the chord PQ is h² + 6h + 15.
(b) Hence find f′(2), explaining your reasoning.
(c) Find the equation of the tangent to the graph at P.
items.markingKey: (a) f(2 + h) expanded (M1 A1); subtract f(2) = 14 and divide by h (M1) AG. (b) as h → 0 the chord gradient → 15 (R1 A1). (c) y − 14 = 15(x − 2) (M1) y = 15x − 16 (A1).

items.stem:
A function f has gradient function f′(x) = −2(x − 4)(x + 2)².
(a) Find the x-coordinates of the stationary points of f.
(b) Determine the nature of each stationary point, justifying your answer.
(c) Given that f(0) = 0, find f(x).
(d) Find f″(x) and verify that f″ is zero at one of the stationary points.
items.answer: (a) x = 4, x = −2 (b) x = 4: local maximum; x = −2: stationary point of inflection (c) f(x) = −x⁴/2 + 12x² + 32x (d) f″(x) = 24 − 6x²; f″(−2) = 0
items.markingKey: (a) f′(x) = 0 (M1) A1 A1 (b) sign of f′ changes + to − at x = 4 (R1 A1); (x − (−2))² ≥ 0 so no sign change at x = −2 (R1 A1) (c) expand f′ and integrate term by term (M1) A1; constant from f(0) (A1) (d) differentiate (M1) A1; substitute (A1) [Total 13 marks]

items.stem:
